section_path: 7.3 Evaluation of Economic, Physical, and Environmental

note: Forty-one measured regions over 26 pages, all accounted: 22 figure rows, 17 printed tables and 2 exclusions (the two display equations on p24). This paper numbers nothing - no 'Figure 1', no 'Table 1' - so every exhibit carries numbering `none`, nine tables carry no caption at all, and the only captions that print at all are the five 'Figure'/Figure.' lines on p17, p20, p22, p25 and p33, the last repeated over the five beta blocks. Two tables (the province ranking p18-p19 and the province numbering p22-p23) run across a page break and record `continued`. No exhibit is cited by number anywhere in the prose, so every mention block is empty. One declared gap: p36 prints two 4x4 AHP judgment matrices (ratios such as 1, 5/6, 5/6, 5/3 and 1, 6/7, 6/4, 6/9) as 108 vector paths, and `fig_extract` returns no measured region on that page at all, so the matrices are recorded as a gap rather than given an invented bbox.
rules: Not one exhibit in this paper carries a number. The caption lines that exist print as bare 'Figure' or 'Figure.' with no digit, and every other exhibit is introduced by prose alone ('the following table shows the results', 'the figure above'), so all 39 counted rows record numbering `none` and every mention block stays empty [caption.numbering].

Nine of the seventeen printed tables have no caption at all - the nomenclature grids, the correlation table, the province rankings and the watershed grid are announced by a heading and a sentence - so those records quote nothing and say so in their notes [caption.verbatim].

Five figure rows are grids the paper prints as figures: the alpha colour scale on p22 and the five beta blocks on p33 are labelled 'Figure' and 'Figure.' and are read as tables inside the figure block, `table-as-figure`, not as plots [geometry.family].

Three tables are drawn as full cell grids - the two terminology glossaries and the neural-network matrix, each with a vertical rule after the symbol column or between every column - while every other table in the paper prints horizontal rules only or, in one case, no rules at all [table.rule_style].

Two measured regions are display equations, not exhibits: the objective function and its constraint set on p24 are the smallest regions on their page (0.025 and 0.009 of the page area) and are excluded rather than recorded [place.area_frac].

Two figure regions hold several charts of one family rather than a mixture: four single-line panels on p11 and three dual-axis panels on p12, so each keeps `line` with a panel count instead of taking `composite-panel` [geometry.panel_count].

Three figure rows are scatter plots of the same annual series with fitted curves drawn over the markers: the markers are the observations and the curves are the fit, so the family follows the markers on all three of the p8 charts [geometry.data_labels].

Four figure rows are maps - the nine watersheds and three terraces on p20, the alpha choropleth on p22 and the six-route transfer map on p25 - of which only the two on p22 and p25 carry any printed numbers, and none carries a scale value or a colour key of its own [geometry.printed_numbers].

Tables split across a page break keep `continued` and say in their note where the header prints, because `header_rows` cannot fall below one in this scheme; the province ranking on p18-p19 and the province numbering on p22-p23 both run that way [table.header_rows].

The paper numbers its headings (2, 3.3.1, 4.2.3, 6.2.5, 7.4.2), so `section_path` quotes the printed heading and `section_numbered` is true throughout - including the notation list, whose heading is simply '2 Nomenclatures' [place.section_numbered].

tables.note: The paper's notation list, ruled as a two-column grid and headed by the section title 'Nomenclatures' rather than by a table caption: 38 printed rows of symbol | definition (D = the fresh water demand of a region, GDP = gross domestic product, omega = the edge weights of the national water transfer network). A rule between every row and no vertical rules. No header row is printed; the header sits in the section heading, so `header_rows` keeps the schema minimum.

The last five rows of the same notation grid, continued over the page break: W_kj, C_kj, COD, cod_kj and B. No header and no repeated section title, so the record keeps `header_rows` at 1 and this note stands for the missing one; two definitions wrap onto a second line inside their cell.

section_path: 3 Model one: Water demand and supply Forecast

tables.note: China's water use 1997-2010, printed as two stacked half-bands because the years will not fit on one line: 'Water 1997 ... 2003' over 5566 ... 5320.4, then 'Water 2004 ... 2010' over 5547.8 ... 6021.99, with the unit '100 million m^3' stacked in the stub. Two year headers, so `header_rows` is 2; horizontal rules only and no vertical rules.

Forecast by three fitting methods: header 'Year | Linear fitting | Power fitting | Interpolant fitting' over thirteen body rows, 2013 to 2025, values 6166.41 to 7028.3. Horizontal rule under the header only, plus the closing rule. The record counts the thirteen data rows and the header; no units are printed in the cells and the unit is stated in the surrounding sentence.

Correlation degrees of the drivers: a bold title row 'Water Consumption Correlation Analysis' spanning all four columns, then 'Factors | Associate degree(1) | Sub-factors | Associate degree(2)'. Three factor blocks with the second column merged across the sub-factor rows (0.9998, 0.9997, 0.3746) and right-hand values 0.9388, 0.9090, 0.6799, 0.7053, 0.9022, 0.7081. The title is printed inside the grid, not as a caption; horizontal rules between blocks only.

The residual analysis of the grey prediction: 'Year | Actual water consumption | Predicted water consumption | Residual Error | Relative Error | Limit Deviation Value' over eleven body rows, 1999 to 2009 (5613.3 / 5484.9 / 128.5 / 0.0229 / 0.0176 for the first). Header words wrap onto three lines inside their cells; no rules are drawn in this band, the grid is held by alignment alone.

The tail of the 2013-2025 forecast, printed transposed: 'Water Consumption' over 6143.9 to 6449.1, then 'Year' over 2020 to 2025, then 'Water Consumption' over 6501.5 to 6770.1. The 2013-2019 block and the table's own header print above the measured band on p15 and are counted here; horizontal rules only.

The head of the province ranking: 'Province | CV | delta O | eta', three body rows (Ningxia 0.206058 / 4.77 / 7.030023, Beijing, Tianjin) with the province column shaded pale blue. The header prints just above the measured band and is counted in `rows`; thin horizontal rules only. The ranking runs onto p19.

The same ranking continued: seventeen rows from Shanghai to Jiangxi with the province column shaded along a pale-blue-to-orange gradient that tracks the CV order. No header is repeated on this page - `header_rows` keeps the schema minimum and this note stands for it. Watermarks cross the right-hand columns; the shading is decoration, not a separate exhibit.

The province numbering for the model, printed two rows at a time with no grid: a header row 'Province' with thirteen names and an index row 'i' under it. The measured band holds rows for indices 9-16; the indices 1-8 row prints immediately above it and is counted with this record, which stays `continued` because the table runs on to p23. Several province names wrap inside their narrow cells ('Shanx i', 'Heilo ngjia ng').

The same numbering continued over the page break: indices 17-24, 25-31 and a trailing row of names with an empty last cell (Yunnan through Xinjiang). No header is repeated at the top of p23, so `header_rows` keeps the schema minimum and this note stands for it.

The worked Beijing example: five province columns (Hunan, Jiangxi, Fujian, Sichuan, Guizhou) over five rows - d_i,1 distance, b_i, c_i, delta w and the relative efficiency eta (0.10968278 down to 0.084805997). Borderless: no vertical and no horizontal rules, alignment alone, which is why the header row prints above the first measured rule. The row label printed 'c_i' disagrees with the model's own symbol e_i.

section_path: 4.3.4 Objective Function of water transfer strategy

tables.note: The desalination notation list: D0, Theta, T, p, p0, t_opt and sigma against their definitions, printed under the heading '5.2 Terminology'. A rule after the symbol column and between every row - the only cells in this paper drawn with a vertical rule besides the pollution glossary and the strategy table. No caption and no header row.

The pollution-control notation list under '6.2.3 Terminology': gamma_k, alpha_k, the three water-quality grades I, II and III, rho_k, mu_k,j, W_kj, C_kj, COD and cod_kj, eleven rows with a vertical rule after the symbol column and a rule between rows. No caption, no header row.

The watershed data and solution: header row of the nine basins over the index row k = 1..9, then rho_k as percentages (43.1% to 90.3%), D_k and W_k in 10^8 m^3, and the dimensionless alpha_k and gamma_k. Nine data columns; horizontal rules only. The region measures the six printed rows below the header, which prints just above it and is counted in `rows`.

The Hai watershed worked in three cities - Datong, Beijing, Tianjin - over three rows: water consumption and water resources in 10^8 m^3 and the formula stub alpha_kj / W_kj times a decreasing sum. The city header prints just above the measured band and is counted in `rows`; horizontal rules only, units carried in the row stubs.

The neural-network input matrix: five strategy rows (Three Gorges Reservoir, the South-North Water Transfer Project, Tianjin Dagang Desalination Plant, Taihu Lake Sewage Treatment, Others) against the five impact columns e_c_i, ph_i, en_i, others_i, de_i, rated 1 to 10, the Others row carrying ellipses. A full cell grid, vertical and horizontal rules, header cell over the strategy column left blank; the note '(All various numerical range is 1-10)' prints under the grid.
